rubric:
1. Proposes LoRA (or similar adapter) fine-tunes over one shared base model, and explains the memory arithmetic: one base model in GPU memory plus many small adapters, instead of one replica per customer.
2. Describes batching across tenants: requests for different adapters share one batch through the base model, with per-request adapter application (multi-LoRA kernels such as those in S-LoRA or Punica style systems), plus continuous batching and a paged KV cache.
3. Handles adapter placement and loading: an adapter cache in GPU memory with eviction (LRU), CPU memory and object storage as lower tiers, routing customers to replicas that already hold their adapter, and dedicated replicas or a merged model for the few heaviest customers.
4. Addresses fairness and isolation: per-tenant quotas and rate limits, fair queuing so heavy tenants cannot starve light ones, no sharing of prefix-cache blocks across tenants (or only for truly public prefixes), and per-tenant data and adapter access control.
5. Covers cost and operations: per-tenant token accounting, autoscaling on queue depth and cache usage, latency SLOs per tier, and evaluating each new adapter before it serves traffic.
